message.content:
The last common ancestor of a lion (Panthera leo) and a zebra (Equus quagga) is a **placental mammal** that lived roughly 70–80 million years ago.  
It was a small, insect‑eating mammal that gave rise to the two distinct lineages that eventually became the order Carnivora (lion) and the order Perissodactyla (zebra).
